title: [weak self] in Stored Closures

docs.title: ARC — Strong Reference Cycles for Closures

hints: A stored closure that captures `self` strongly creates a cycle.
Add a capture list with `weak self` and unwrap it at the start of the closure.
`onTick = { [weak self] in guard let self else { return }; count += 1; log.lines.append("tick \(count)") }`.
jsBridge: A class storing a closure that captures `self` strongly is the #1 Swift leak. `[weak self]` breaks the cycle. JS never needs this because GC handles it, but in Swift you must think about capture ownership.

compass.q: `this.onTick = () => this.count++` never leaks in JS. Why does the Swift equivalent leak?
`[weak self]` + `guard let self` vs `[unowned self]`: when is `unowned` acceptable?
Do non-escaping closures (like `map`) need `[weak self]`? Does `Task { }` retain self? Until when?
Combine `sink { self.x = $0 }` stored in `cancellables` is the same cycle. How do you fix it?
